messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Subject: BrightPath follow-up: model fit notes + prompt collection request

Hi Sara — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and clear next steps so we stay aligned.

Recap from today's demo / discovery:
- Primary goal: replace manual tagging and entity normalization in BrightPath's ingestion pipeline for customer support transcripts (high precision on entities, must preserve PHI redaction).
- Latency target: P99 < 300ms for short completions (single-turn entity extraction).
- Volume: ~8M short inference calls/month with burst patterns during EMEA business hours.
- Security: VPC-private deployment preferred; SOC2 evidence requested during procurement.

Initial Redwood model fit recommendations (from today):
- Candidate (low-latency, good instruction-following): redwood-3b-instruct-quant (recommended for PoC to validate extraction quality and latency).
- Candidate (higher quality, fallback for edge cases): redwood-13b-qa (use for batched reprocessing where latency is less critical).

What we need from BrightPath to move the eval forward:
1) Prompt set: a representative sample of 200–500 real prompts (customer transcripts) including edge cases and examples requiring redaction. Please use the attached prompt_template.csv for formatting.
2) Redaction guidance: any company-specific PII/PHI rules we must apply (we included a suggested redaction guide; please update and return).
3) Priority intents / golden outputs for ~50 high-value examples so we can compute precision/recall automatically.
4) Procurement contact for SOC2 and contract path (cc'ing Ben for handoff).

Attachments: prompt_template.csv (CSV with columns: id, original_text, expected_output, privacy_tags), redaction_guidelines.pdf (our suggested defaults).

Next steps: If you confirm we can receive example prompts under your standard data-sharing NDA, we will:
- Spin up a private eval in your preferred region (us-west) with redwood-3b-instruct-quant and redwood-13b-qa,
- Run automated metrics (precision/recall, redaction recall, latency P50/P95/P99),
- Return a short eval report and recommended model/profile within 3 business days of receiving the dataset.

Can you confirm who will upload the prompt CSV vs which examples we should collect from the S3 ingestion bucket? Also, does procurement need a finalized SOC2 pack before we start the PoC evaluation, or is a shared SOC2 attestation sufficient?

Thanks — Camila

--

Thanks Camila — really helpful recap. A few clarifications and our responses below.

We can provide the prompts under our existing NDA (no new legal required). Procurement looped in to confirm SOC2 logistics.

On the prompt set: we'll start with a curated set of ~300 transcripts pulled from the last quarter and flag ~60 edge/ambiguous cases. We'll use your template and then upload to the secure Drive folder you shared. Two notes on redaction:
- We need to preserve partial account numbers for troubleshooting (last 4 digits ok) but redaction is required for full SSNs, credit card numbers, and health PHIs.
- Customer names must be tokenized, but BrightPath needs a reversible mapping for our internal debug only (we can provide mapping under separate secure key exchange).

Priority golden outputs: we'll attach 50 gold examples in the same CSV.

Attachment: I attached our initial prompt dump (preview-120.csv) — it's just a sample. Please note we scrubbed obvious PHI; the full file will be uploaded to your Drive link.

On procurement: procurement confirms shared SOC2 summary is fine to start PoC; they will request the full report during contract negotiation.

Thanks — Sara
